answer_text:
Let

\[
x_0=\frac{2}{15},\qquad x_{n+1}=f(x_n).
\]

Then \(f_n\left(\frac{2}{15}\right)=x_n\).

Compute the first few iterates:

\[
x_1=f\left(\frac{2}{15}\right)=\frac{2}{15}+\frac12=\frac{19}{30}.
\]

Since \(\frac{19}{30}>\frac12\),

\[
x_2=f\left(\frac{19}{30}\right)=2\left(1-\frac{19}{30}\right)=\frac{11}{15}.
\]

Again \(\frac{11}{15}>\frac12\), so

\[
x_3=f\left(\frac{11}{15}\right)=2\left(1-\frac{11}{15}\right)=\frac{8}{15}.
\]

Then

\[
x_4=f\left(\frac{8}{15}\right)=2\left(1-\frac{8}{15}\right)=\frac{14}{15}.
\]

Finally,

\[
x_5=f\left(\frac{14}{15}\right)=2\left(1-\frac{14}{15}\right)=\frac{2}{15}=x_0.
\]

Thus the iterates are periodic with period \(5\). Since

\[
2006=5\cdot 401+1,
\]

we have

\[
f_{2006}\left(\frac{2}{15}\right)=x_{2006}=x_1=\frac{19}{30}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{19}{30}}
